newsitem.title: USA: U.S. has no comment on Netanyahu, Ross to meet PM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. has no comment on Netanyahu, Ross to meet PM.

text.p: U.S. National Security Adviser Sandy Berger said on Wednesday he had no comment on a report that police had recommended charging Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with fraud and breach of trust.
Berger, briefing reporters on an unrelated topic, also said that U.S. Middle East special envoy Dennis Ross was in Israel and was expected to meet Netanyahu as scheduled on Wednesday.
Israel's Channel One television reported that police had recommended charging Netanyahu with fraud and breach of trust in the appointment of an attorney general.
Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak told the television: "So far as I know it's not correct and in any event the one to decide on submission of indictments is the prosecution and not the police."

Israel Radio later quoted Israeli public security minister Avigdor Kahalani, whose ministry is responsible for the police, as confirming the television report that police recommended bringing charges although the state prosecutor could decide to ignore the recommendation.

Asked about the television report, Berger replied: "I have seen the report ... but this is an internal matter involving the Israeli government and the Israeli judicial system and I don't think it's appropriate for me to comment on it."

Berger, who was speaking to reporters before the Israel Radio report, added: "Dennis Ross is in Israel. He will go forward with his meetings. He will be meeting with the prime minister, I believe today."
